html:
A famine that struck the Deccan plateau and Gujarat in western India from 1630 to 1632, early in the reign of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan. Millions died.

It began with failed rains and crop failures several seasons running. War made it worse: Shah Jahan's armies were campaigning in the Deccan against Ahmadnagar and other sultanates, taking grain and fodder. Hunger brought disease, and people fled their villages in great numbers. Mughal officials opened soup kitchens and cut taxes, but relief reached few.

The famine is well known partly because European traders saw it. English and Dutch merchants at Surat wrote of empty towns and roads lined with the dead; the English traveller Peter Mundy described it as he passed through. Trade from Gujarat collapsed for years, since the weavers who made the cloth for export had died or fled. This hit the East India Company hard and helped push it to look further east, toward the Coromandel coast and Bengal.
sum: A famine that struck the Deccan plateau and Gujarat in western India from 1630 to 1632, early in the reign of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan. Millions died.
